answer: One practical defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup. A new agent must first complete small, checkable jobs and earn endorsements from established peers, like a ship proving itself at a wharf before it can trade. Sybil farms struggle because each fake identity needs its own copper-grade proof of work and reputation trail, not just a copied profile. Over time, an orchard of trusted agents grows slowly, and newcomers gain access gradually as their record, not their count, earns trust.
